audit_findings.title: JRD closing would invalidate both the earnings claim and share denominator
audit_findings.magnitude: $29.1 billion consideration, including $21.6 billion cash and 91.5 million shares; shares equal 18.3% of the current 499.074075 million denominator
audit_findings.mechanism: Closing would add JRD earnings while adding acquisition interest, hybrid distributions and 91.5 million shares to the OE numerator and per-share denominator.
audit_findings.evidence: Sysco has agreed to pay approximately $29.1 billion to JRD equity holders, comprised of $21.6 billion in cash, subject to customary adjustments, and 91.5 million shares of Sysco Holdings common stock.
audit_findings.explanation: No present valuation error is demonstrated because the AS_FILED valuation explicitly excludes the unclosed acquisition. Closing would fundamentally change the valued business and could move value either way, but it is forward-looking and not presently in the filed perimeter.
audit_findings.action: At closing, replace the current valuation with a combined-company rerun using actual financing costs, hybrid terms, fully diluted Holdco shares and seasoned combined owner earnings.

audit_findings.title: Deal failure carries an unmodeled $1.164 billion cash claim
audit_findings.magnitude: $1.164 billion, equal to $2.33 per current diluted share and 4.5% of base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: If payable, the termination fee reduces cash or creates financing needs and associated interest costs in the equity bridge and OE.
audit_findings.evidence: If the Merger Agreement is terminated due to a failure to obtain required regulatory clearances or because the mergers are not consummated by the termination date set forth in the Merger Agreement, Sysco has agreed to pay the JRD holder representative a termination fee of $ 1.164 billion.
audit_findings.explanation: The fee is a filed contingent obligation, but no current liability or valuation error is demonstrated because payment requires specified deal-failure circumstances. If paid, it would lower value, although the $2.33-per-share direct effect would not reverse the present price-versus-value conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Create a separate deal-failure trigger; upon qualifying termination, reduce cash by the fee, include remaining transaction costs and rerun for any financing interest.

audit_findings.title: The latest-year anchor may perpetuate transaction-specific one-offs
audit_findings.mechanism: Retained nonrecurring legal, bridge-financing, rate-lock, acquisition, restructuring or transformation charges depress anchor OE; removing costs that are recurring or economically necessary would inflate OE and growth.
audit_findings.evidence: Fiscal year 2026 results of operations also remove the impact of a charge associated with a legal matter, amortization expense associated with debt issuance costs on a bridge loan facility, and a loss on deal contingent rate lock transactions entered into to mitigate interest rate risk on future permanent debt that could potentially be issued to finance the purchase of Jetro Restaurant Depot.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing identifies $603 million of pretax Certain Items across restructuring/transformation/legal costs, acquisition-related costs, bridge amortization and rate-lock losses, with a $458 million after-tax non-GAAP adjustment. The record does not show how each item entered the $1,719.9 million OE anchor, and those totals cannot be treated wholesale as an OE correction because they include potentially recurring costs and possible overlap with D&A treatment. A current classification issue is demonstrated, but its net valuation effect and materiality remain unresolved.
audit_findings.action: Reconstruct FY2026 OE line by line, documenting the treatment and tax effect of each Certain Item, then rerun only with independently supported recurring-versus-nonrecurring classifications.

audit_findings.title: Sale-leaseback proceeds could be mistaken for recurring owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: maximum $176 million, 10.2% of anchor OE; if fully removed, computed bull value falls from $60.74 to approximately $54.90 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: Using asset-sale proceeds as an offset to maintenance capital expenditure would raise OE through a nonrecurring financing-like inflow while future lease expense remains.
audit_findings.evidence: During fiscal 2026, we received $176 million in proceeds from sales of plant and equipment, which was primarily attributable to proceeds received from sale leaseback transactions.
audit_findings.explanation: Whether the $176 million was used in the OE calculation is unresolved. Even under the conservative maximum assumption that all proceeds improperly increased anchor OE, the correction lowers every scenario and leaves the approximately $54.90 bull value well below the $80.05 market price, so it cannot reverse the current valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Trace the FY2026 maintenance-capex input; if it used the filed $524 million net-capex figure, rerun with $700 million gross additions while retaining all resulting lease expense.

audit_findings.title: The cash add-back is stale after a material post-year-end repayment
audit_findings.magnitude: up to $1.0 billion, equal to $2.00 per current diluted share and 3.9% of base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Cash spent after year-end must leave the equity bridge; replacement commercial paper preserves cash only by creating prospective interest expense in equity-level OE.
audit_findings.evidence: In July 2026, Sysco repaid $ 1.0 billion of matured senior notes that were classified within current maturities of long-term debt as of June 27, 2026.
audit_findings.explanation: Use of the June 27 cash balance on September 5 without reconciliation is a demonstrated date mismatch. The exact overstatement is unresolved because $1.363 billion of commercial paper was outstanding by August 4. Even a full $1.0 billion cash reduction would lower bull value only from $60.74 to about $58.74, further below the $80.05 price rather than changing the conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Replace the bridge with September 5 cash and short-term investments, reconcile the July repayment to post-year-end commercial paper, and include prospective interest on any replacement borrowing.

audit_findings.title: Unfunded retirement claims may not be cash-consistent with OE
audit_findings.magnitude: $317 million SERP obligation, equal to $0.64 per current diluted share and 1.2% of base equity value; expected FY2027 SERP payments are $32 million
audit_findings.mechanism: Any retirement cash burden not already represented in OE must reduce OE or the equity bridge, without double-counting pension expense and benefit payments.
audit_findings.evidence: As of June 27, 2026 and June 28, 2025, the SERP had benefit obligations of $ 317 million and $ 333 million, respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: Cash inconsistency is possible but not demonstrated. The filing records the pension liabilities and discloses $32 million of expected FY2027 SERP payments. Even deducting the entire $317 million obligation from equity would reduce bull value only to about $60.10 per share, still far below $80.05; the $88 million of related life-insurance assets would make the net exposure smaller before considering other trust assets.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile OE pension expense to expected SERP and international-plan cash payments and identify related trust assets; adjust only for cash burdens not already captured.

audit_findings.title: Unidentified D&A is conservatively left in owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: $776.7 million aggregate historical residual: FY2017 $714.5 million, FY2018 $36.0 million and FY2022 $26.2 million; $0 direct FY2026 anchor add-back identified
audit_findings.mechanism: Eligible residual D&A would increase historical OE and could affect the computed trend, but it does not directly increase the latest-year OE used as the anchor.
audit_findings.evidence: identified eligible D&A is below the filed composite; residual is conservatively left as an expense, not added back: FY2017 $714.5m (79.2% of filed D&A); FY2018 $36.0m (4.7% of filed D&A); FY2022 $26.2m (3.4% of filed D&A)
audit_findings.explanation: The treatment is conservative rather than a demonstrated overstatement. The supplied residuals concern prior years, while the selected $1,719.9 million anchor is FY2026 and is already below the $2,112 million trend by $392.1 million. No FY2026 residual is identified, so the supplied amounts have no direct effect on the current anchor or valuation scenarios.
audit_findings.action: Classify the residual D&A from filed schedules; if eligible amounts are established, recompute the trend and confirm that the MIN(trend, latest) rule still selects FY2026 OE before changing the valuation.
